doc.title: Wendy Oxenhorn — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Housing assistance after Katrina
summary: Her caseload grows from 500 to 1500 musicians, and renting without pay stubs is a barrier.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: There’s also a Housing Emergency Assistance program. You’ve discussed the impact of it, but not the specifics.

Again, that really... We kind of exploded because of Katrina. There was such a need. We went from 500 musicians a year to 1500. It wasn’t just one family would be one case. You’d find someone, they’re in a dome somewhere, they need an apartment. Try to rent an apartment when you don’t have a pay stub. You worked on Bourbon Street or you were in a brass band on the streets? There were no pay stubs.
